problem: Deep RL navigation agents trained in simulation transfer poorly to the real world because of the reality gap. Standard remedies (higher-fidelity simulation, domain randomisation) add training cost, and self-attention has not been explored for bridging the gap in 3D navigation.
motivation: Humans ignore task-irrelevant visual information (inattentional blindness). An agent that acts only on the most important image patches should be more robust to visual differences between simulation and the real world. Self-attention is also very parameter-efficient, which allows neuroevolution training and use on constrained hardware.
key_idea: Adapt the Tang et al. 2020 self-attention patch-selection bottleneck agent, which acts only on the locations of the top-K patches and is trained by CMA-ES neuroevolution, to 3D maze navigation in DeepMind Lab, then apply the simulation-trained patch ranker to real-world images.
insight: A bottleneck that keeps only the locations of the top-K patches yields policies with under 4000 parameters that transfer across mazes with different visual appearance. Ablations show depth input shifts selection from wall/floor colour contrasts towards structure, and non-overlapping patches (M3, S8) generalise better. A smaller K gives higher training scores but overfits, and training in the harder NavMazeRandomGoal03 gives better generalisation. Exploration reward speeds learning about 2x (about 4x in RandomGoal03) but lowers final scores, and collision penalties cause 'stuck in place' behaviour.
method: Environment: DeepMind Lab NavMazeStatic01 / NavMazeRandomGoal03; 64x64xC observations (C=1 to 4: RGB, RGB-D, depth-only, gray+depth); 3-D action space (look, strafe, move); frame skip 4, 60 s episodes (900 observations)
Patch partitioning: sliding-window patches of size M with stride S, flattened into a matrix X of size n x d_in; depth is converted to disparity
Self-attention ranking: learnable W_k and W_q (d_in x d) with softmax act as an importance vote per patch; only the top-K patches are kept
Feature retrieval: only the (x,y) locations of the K selected patches are passed on, not their pixel content
Controller: single-layer 16-cell LSTM followed by a fully connected layer producing normalised action values, interpolated and rounded to the action ranges

Training: CMA-ES neuroevolution, 1200 generations, population 64, 8 episodes per member, with a decoupled FIFO task queue for distributed workers; rewards are goal 10, apple 1, exploration r_expl 0.1 and optional collision penalty p_col
Real-world test: the sim-trained attention module is run on real images and video, and K can be changed at inference time

setting.backbone: Self-attention patch selector + 16-cell LSTM controller (trained from scratch via CMA-ES)
setting.training_data: DeepMind Lab NavMazeStatic01 or NavMazeRandomGoal03 simulation episodes, under 0.1E9 environment steps; no extra data
setting.action_space: 3-D continuous-valued actions (look left/right, strafe left/right, move forward/backward), rounded to integers

numbers_note: Results are given only as boxplots (scores over 200 trials per environment) and qualitative figures; the text states only that scores above 60 in NavMazeStatic01 were reached with under 0.1E9 steps. No table of metrics.
results: Agents reached scores above 60 in NavMazeStatic01 with under 0.1E9 steps and under 4000 parameters. They generalised to other DML mazes with different appearance, and the learned patch selection highlights task-relevant regions in real-world images, shown qualitatively. No real-robot navigation or baseline comparison is reported.
limitations: Real-world evaluation is qualitative (patch visualisation on images/video); there is no closed-loop navigation on a real robot and no quantitative metrics or baselines
Using only patch locations limits the LSTM controller's input and performance; a smaller K overfits
Results come only from DeepMind Lab mazes with boxplots, and the hyperparameter analysis is largely qualitative
builds_on: Tang et al. 2020 (attention agent: Neuroevolution of self-interpretable agents)
